Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: Digital authentication is a core function: NIN is used as a digital identifier across 45+ institutions. NIDA's new SDIS includes an Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) for real-time biometric authentication. The new digital ID supports remote identity verification via fingerprint, iris, or face. SIM registration regulation (2024) mandates biometric verification against NIDA records. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: Irembo (Rwanda's national e-government portal, launched 2015) requires NIN for access to 90+ government services including national ID applications, civil registration certificates, and judicial services via IECMS. The SDIS integrates Irembo as a core service delivery platform. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: CIS/RIA Digital ID evaluation (2021) found that neither the ID law nor NIDA law provides rights for data subjects to access, confirm or correct information in the national ID database. Once registered, individuals are not aware of the full content stored. Law No. 058/2021 grants general data subject rights (Art. 20 portability, Art. 19 rectification) but implementation for the ID database is not documented. Value=1 (No formal individual data access mechanism confirmed for the ID database).

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Banks and telecoms sign MoUs with NIDA to access the NID database for KYC. RURA Regulation No. 18/R/SM-ICT/RURA/2024 mandates biometric SIM card registration using NIDA verification. National Bank of Rwanda KYC guidelines require identity verification against government databases. eKYC using NIDA integration is standard practice. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Rwanda's general court system provides recourse for ID-related grievances through administrative review before NIDA and subsequently administrative courts. The Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS) for judiciary requires NIN authentication. Law No. 058/2021 grants data subjects appeal rights to the supervisory authority (NCSA). However, no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism exists. Value=2 (Yes but not ID-specific).

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: The NCI-CRVS system (launched Aug 2020) assigns a unique NIN at birth and integrates directly and in real-time with the National Population Registry. Over 600 health facilities, 2,148 cells and 416 sector offices offer real-time birth/death registration linked to NIDA's NPR. Birth registration completeness reached 92.9% in 2022. Value=3 (Full integration).

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Cabinet approved the National Data Sharing Policy (May 2025) establishing a secure framework for inter-agency data exchange compliant with Law No. 058/2021. NIDA uses MoUs with 45+ institutions for database access. However, formal rules governing private-sector data sharing remain partial—MoUs are not enshrined in binding legislation. Value=2 (Partially available).

Comments: Law No. 029/2023 of 14/06/2023 specifically governs population registration in the National Single Digital Identity System (SDIS). Ministerial Order N° 001/MINICT/24 of 22/01/2024 relates to the Single Digital Identity Coordination Council. Value=2 (Yes).

Comments: Law No. 058/2021 of 13/10/2021 relating to the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy entered into force on 15 October 2021. The National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) is the designated supervisory authority. Value=2 (Yes).

Comments: Law No. 058/2021 designates the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) as the supervisory authority with powers to oversee implementation, issue registration certificates to data controllers/processors, and impose administrative sanctions. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: Law No. 14/2008 makes possession and carrying of the national identity card obligatory for every Rwandan aged 16 and above. The NIN/National ID is the primary legal proof of identity accepted for healthcare, higher education, taxation, pensions, social assistance, financial services, and travel within EAC (Kenya, Uganda). Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Rwanda has a comprehensive legal framework: Law No. 14/2008 (amended 2018) governing national ID; Law No. 43/2011 establishing NIDA; Law No. 029/2023 governing population registration in the Single Digital Identity System; and Law No. 058/2021 on Data Protection and Privacy. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: NIDA is an established in-country government institution (Law No. 43/2011) that manages the NPR and ID card issuance domestically. However, the new SDIS ($57M project) was developed under the World Bank Rwanda Digital Acceleration Project (RDAP), with significant external technical support. The ABIS and new digital infrastructure involve international vendors. Value=2 (Partial in-country).

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: NIDA is under administrative supervision of the Ministry of Local Government (MINALOC), not the Ministry of Finance (MINECOFIN). The SDIS project ($57M) is financed through the World Bank Rwanda Digital Acceleration Project (RDAP), with government budget allocation of ~$8.5M for 2025-2026. MINECOFIN oversees general public finance; no dedicated Ministry of Finance ID-specific oversight mandate identified beyond standard budgetary control. Value=2 (Partial).

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: NIDA historically covered operating costs from service fees (first card: RWF 500; replacements: RWF 1,500)—described as 'sustainable self-sufficient' in the World Bank 2018 ID4D Diagnostic. However, the new SDIS ($57M) is primarily funded by the World Bank RDAP grant/loan with ~$8.5M domestic government allocation. Sustainability is mixed at this development phase. Value=2 (Mixed).

Comments: The new Single Digital ID (SDIS) collects ten fingerprints, iris scans, and facial recognition (launched Aug 2025). The legacy system already collected two thumbprints and a photograph. Xinhua reported iris scans and fingerprints for the new e-ID. Value=3 (Facial/Iris).

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Rwanda's National Population Registry (NPR) and NID database have been fully digital since 2008 following the door-to-door census and biometric capture campaign. No paper-only records for the current system; the new SDIS is 100% digital. Value=3 (Digital).

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Rwanda has a long-standing national ID system (NIDA, est. 2011) with full nationwide physical ID card deployment (>98% eligible adults). A new Single Digital ID (SDIS/e-Indangamuntu) is under active nationwide rollout—enrollment started Oct 2025, 1.8M biometrics captured by Feb 2026, card issuance expected Jun 2026. Rated 4 (partially deployed) as the new digital form factor is mid-rollout.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The SDIS is designed with interoperability at its core: the platform integrates NIDA, Irembo e-government portal, Rwanda Social Security Board, Rwanda Revenue Authority, Ministry of Education, and Ministry of Local Government. The NCI-CRVS system links civil registration directly to the NPR via a unique ID number at birth. MoUs with 45+ institutions for database access are documented. Rwanda's Cabinet approved a National Data Sharing Policy (May 2025).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: National ID (NID/NIN) is mandatory for opening bank accounts in Rwanda. Banks must conduct KYC using National ID under National Bank of Rwanda regulations. The ID4D diagnostic notes NID is required for financial services. The SDIS is designed to facilitate banking access. Value=3 (Mandatory).

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The first national ID card costs RWF 500 (~USD 0.50). Replacements cost RWF 1,500 (~USD 1.50). There is a fee, so the credential is not free. Value=1 (No—not free; fee applies).

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Comments: Rwanda's national ID is a formally recognized travel document with Kenya and Uganda under the Northern Corridor Integration Projects (NCIP) since January 2014, enabling travel for up to six months. Kenya-Rwanda launched a mutual digital ID verification system at Gatuna One-Stop Border Post (June 2024) for trade and business. Plans to extend to Uganda and Tanzania. Value=3 (Formally interoperable).

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Current law (Law No. 14/2008, amended 2018) mandates ID at age 16. The new SDIS (Law No. 029/2023) extends enrollment to include newborns at birth via the CRVS-linked NPR system, with physical card issuance beginning at 16. Children under 5 receive a photograph during SDIS enrollment. NIDA stated the new digital ID 'will be issued from birth.' The NPR captures children below 16. For the national ID card (credential), eligibility remains 16+. Value=1 (>17 for credential; enrollment at birth for the registry is a transition in progress).

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Law No. 14/2008 states: 'Possession of and carrying the national identity card is obligatory to every Rwandan aged sixteen (16) and above.' Enrollment and possession are mandatory for all eligible Rwandans. Value=3 (Mandatory for all).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: National ID is required for Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI/Mutuelle de Santé) enrollment and healthcare access. World Bank report confirms NID is required for 'healthcare.' SDIS is designed to improve healthcare service delivery. Birth registration via NCI-CRVS issues NIN at birth for healthcare purposes. Value=3 (Mandatory).

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Rwanda issues ID cards to registered refugees, foreign residents, asylum seekers, migrants, and stateless persons. NIDA's SDIS enrollment (2025-2026) explicitly includes 'citizens living abroad, foreign residents, refugees, asylum seekers, migrants, stateless persons.' Refugees receive NIDA ID cards valid as Rwandan IDs. Value=3 (All non-nationals included).

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: NIDA estimates >98% of the eligible population (16+) have been issued a national ID card. The NPR captures approximately 98% of the total population. World Bank People's Perspectives report (2021) confirms this figure. Value=5 (>89%).

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: NIDA requires institutions connecting to the NID database to observe 'certain security standards and certification' (MoU requirement). The National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) oversees data protection compliance. The SDIS includes PKI infrastructure and ABIS security features. Rwanda's Auditor General (2025) reviewed NIDA's ID management processes. No public external security audit specifically of the ID system was identified, but government-wide security review mechanisms exist. Value=2 (Yes—security reviews conducted through NCSA oversight and NIDA certification requirements).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: RURA Regulation No. 18/R/SM-ICT/RURA/2024 (Aug 2024) mandates that all SIM card holders must register using National ID with biometric verification against NIDA records. Biometric SIM registration pilot was launched in Sep 2024. The regulation explicitly states 'The SIM card registration shall have the same KYC as NIDA database.' Value=3 (Mandatory).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: National ID is mandatory for accessing social protection services. The Ubudehe social register is linked to the NIN for targeting safety net programs. Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB) uses NIN. World Bank report confirms NID is required for 'social assistance' and government services. Value=3 (Mandatory).
